tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common

/-!
# Access kernel: preservation by `enterFrame` and `exitFrame`

Operations O6 `enterFrame` (§72) and O7 `exitFrame` (§73) of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, with the frame rules of §39 and the parameter and
reanchoring rules of §45. Both steps preserve the kernel invariant of §57 (`KInv`) and, separately,
the auxiliary invariant `KAux`. The file also proves entry protection of parameters (§72.3 and
the last paragraph of §72), the release of authorities whose holder dies at the exit (§73
effect, §39), the absence of dangling authorities after the exit (§73, §54), reanchoring to the
first surviving active origin (§73.4, §73 effect), and determinism of both steps (§58).

Helper lemmas live in the namespace `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Frames`.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

namespace Frames

/-! ## Lists -/

/-- Indices of `List.range` are strictly increasing (§72: identities of the root locals). -/
theorem range_pairwise_lt : ∀ n, (List.range n).Pairwise (· < ·)
  | 0 => by simp
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [List.range_succ, List.pairwise_append]
    refine ⟨range_pairwise_lt n, List.pairwise_singleton _ _, fun a ha b hb => ?_⟩
    rw [List.mem_singleton] at hb; subst hb; exact List.mem_range.1 ha

/-- In a strictly increasing list, a value sits at one index only (§72: identities of the root
locals). -/
theorem getElem?_inj_of_lt : ∀ {l : List Nat} {i j x : Nat}, l.Pairwise (· < ·) →
    l[i]? = some x → l[j]? = some x → i = j
  | [], _, _, _, _, h, _ => by simp at h
  | _ :: _, 0, 0, _, _, _, _ => rfl
  | _ :: l, 0, j + 1, x, hp, hi, hj => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at hi; subst hi
    have := (List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).1 _ (List.mem_of_getElem? hj)
    exact absurd this (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
  | _ :: l, i + 1, 0, x, hp, hi, hj => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at hj; subst hj
    have := (List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).1 _ (List.mem_of_getElem? hi)
    exact absurd this (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
  | _ :: l, i + 1, j + 1, x, hp, hi, hj => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_succ] at hi hj
    rw [getElem?_inj_of_lt (List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).2 hi hj]

/-- A member of a list sits at some index (§72: the root locals). -/
theorem exists_getElem?_of_mem {α : Type} {a : α} : ∀ {l : List α}, a ∈ l →
    ∃ k : Nat, l[k]? = some a
  | b :: l, h => by
    rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
    · exact ⟨0, rfl⟩
    · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_getElem?_of_mem h; exact ⟨k + 1, by simpa using hk⟩

/-- An element of the mapped suffix of an appended list has an index (§72: the root authorities
of the locals). -/
theorem append_map_get {α β : Type} (A₀ : List β) (g : α → β) {l : List α} {a : α} (h : a ∈ l) :
    ∃ j, (A₀ ++ l.map g)[A₀.length + j]? = some (g a) := by
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := exists_getElem?_of_mem h
  exact ⟨j, by rw [List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_add_right _ _), Nat.add_sub_cancel_left,
    List.getElem?_map, hj]; rfl⟩

/-! ## Shapes of locals (§72.2) -/

/-- A local shape has as many elements as its shape (§72). -/
theorem toShape_length (ls : LocalShape) : ls.toShape.length = ls.length := by
  simp [LocalShape.toShape]

/-- No local has an owning element (§72, §39: locals are owned by the new frame). -/
theorem toShape_owner (ls : LocalShape) (i : Nat) : (ls.toShape[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = none := by
  simp only [LocalShape.toShape, List.getElem?_map]; cases ls[i]? <;> rfl

/-- Every local is owned by the receiving holder (§72 `ok` effect, §39). -/
theorem shapeOwner_toShape (ls : LocalShape) (hd : Holder) (i : Nat) :
    shapeOwner ls.toShape hd i = hd := by
  simp only [shapeOwner, toShape_owner]

/-- Root locals are elements of the shape without parent (§40, §72). -/
theorem rootIdx_mem {ls : LocalShape} {k i : Nat} (h : (rootIdx ls.toShape)[k]? = some i) :
    i < ls.length ∧ (ls.toShape[i]?).bind (·.1) = none := by
  have := List.mem_of_getElem? h
  simp only [rootIdx, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, Option.isNone_iff_eq_none] at this
  rw [toShape_length] at this; exact this

/-- An element without parent is a root local (§40, §72). -/
theorem mem_rootIdx {ls : LocalShape} {k : Nat} (hk : k < ls.length)
    (hn : (ls.toShape[k]?).bind (·.1) = none) : k ∈ rootIdx ls.toShape := by
  simp only [rootIdx, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, toShape_length, hk, hn,
    Option.isNone_none, and_self]

/-- Root locals have distinct positions (§72: one root authority per root local). -/
theorem rootIdx_inj {ls : LocalShape} {k k' i : Nat} (h : (rootIdx ls.toShape)[k]? = some i)
    (h' : (rootIdx ls.toShape)[k']? = some i) : k = k' :=
  getElem?_inj_of_lt ((range_pairwise_lt _).filter _) h h'

/-- The parent of a local is an earlier local (§72.2, `ShapeOK`). -/
theorem shape_parent {n : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (hsh : ShapeOK n ls.toShape) {i r : Nat}
    (hi : i < ls.length) (hr : (ls.toShape[i]?).bind (·.1) = some r) : n ≤ r ∧ r < n + i := by
  have := (hsh i (List.mem_range.2 (by rw [toShape_length]; exact hi))).1
  rw [hr] at this; exact ⟨this.1, this.2.1⟩

/-! ## Origin chains and effective anchors (§42, §44) -/

/-- Under the origin order of `WF3` (§49.5), the origin of an authority precedes it. -/
theorem org_lt {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {x o : Nat} (h : s.org x = some o) : o < x := by
  simp only [S3.org] at h
  cases hy : s.A[x]? with
  | none => rw [hy] at h; cases h
  | some y => rw [hy] at h; exact hw.origins x y o hy h

/-- One step of an origin chain (§42): the chain starts with the origin when it is smaller, or
it is empty. -/
theorem ancs_step {s : S3} {x o : Nat} (h : s.org x = some o) :
    (o < x ∧ s.ancs x = o :: s.ancs o) ∨ s.ancs x = [] := by
  by_cases hlt : o < x
  · exact .inl ⟨hlt, chain_cons h hlt⟩
  · right; unfold S3.ancs chain
    cases x with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ k => simp [chainF, h, hlt]

/-- Under the origin order of `WF3` (§49.5), the origin chain of `x` reaches a root authority:
some element of `x` and its ancestors has no origin. -/
theorem reaches_root {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) :
    ∀ n x, x < n → ∃ r, (r = x ∨ r ∈ s.ancs x) ∧ s.org r = none
  | 0, _, h => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, x, hx => by
    cases ho : s.org x with
    | none => exact ⟨x, .inl rfl, ho⟩
    | some o =>
      have hlt := org_lt hw ho
      obtain ⟨r, hr, hro⟩ := reaches_root hw n o (by omega)
      refine ⟨r, .inr ?_, hro⟩
      rw [S3.ancs, chain_cons ho hlt]
      rcases hr with rfl | hr
      · exact List.mem_cons_self ..
      · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hr

/-- On an origin chain, an element without origin comes after every other element (§42). -/
theorem ancs_root_after {s : S3} : ∀ n a, a < n → ∀ y w, y ∈ s.ancs a → w ∈ s.ancs a →
    s.org w = none → w = y ∨ w ∈ s.ancs y
  | 0, _, h, _, _, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, a, ha, y, w, hy, hw, hwo => by
    cases ho : s.org a with
    | none => rw [S3.ancs, chain_none ho] at hy; simp at hy
    | some o =>
      rcases ancs_step ho with ⟨hlt, he⟩ | he
      · rw [he] at hy hw
        rcases List.mem_cons.1 hy with rfl | hy
        · rcases List.mem_cons.1 hw with rfl | hw
          · exact .inl rfl
          · exact .inr hw
        · rcases List.mem_cons.1 hw with rfl | hw
          · rw [S3.ancs, chain_none hwo] at hy; simp at hy
          · exact ancs_root_after n o (by omega) y w hy hw hwo
      · rw [he] at hy; simp at hy

/-- The effective anchor of `x` is `x` or one of its ancestors (§44). -/
theorem effAnchor_mem (s : S3) (x : Nat) : s.effAnchor x = x ∨ s.effAnchor x ∈ s.ancs x :=
  List.mem_cons.1 (List.getLastD_mem_cons (l := s.ancs x) (a := x))

/-- The effective anchor of `x` does not exceed `x` (§44). -/
theorem effAnchor_le (s : S3) (x : Nat) : s.effAnchor x ≤ x := by
  rcases effAnchor_mem s x with h | h
  · exact Nat.le_of_eq h
  · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt h)

/-- The effective anchor of `x` is the element without origin of its chain (§44). -/
theorem effAnchor_eq {s : S3} : ∀ n x, x < n → ∀ r, (r = x ∨ r ∈ s.ancs x) → s.org r = none →
    s.effAnchor x = r
  | 0, _, h, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, x, hx, r, hr, hro => by
    rcases hr with rfl | hr
    · simp [S3.effAnchor, S3.ancs, chain_none hro]
    · cases ho : s.org x with
      | none => rw [S3.ancs, chain_none ho] at hr; simp at hr
      | some o =>
        rcases ancs_step ho with ⟨hlt, he⟩ | he
        · have e : s.effAnchor x = s.effAnchor o := by
            simp only [S3.effAnchor, he, List.getLastD_cons]
          rw [e]; rw [he] at hr
          exact effAnchor_eq n o (by omega) r (List.mem_cons.1 hr) hro
        · rw [he] at hr; simp at hr

/-- Under the origin order of `WF3` (§49.5), the effective anchor has no origin (§44). -/
theorem effAnchor_root {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (x : Nat) : s.org (s.effAnchor x) = none := by
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hro⟩ := reaches_root hw (x + 1) x (Nat.lt_succ_self x)
  rw [effAnchor_eq (x + 1) x (Nat.lt_succ_self x) r hr hro]; exact hro

/-- The effective anchor depends only on the origin chain (§44). -/
theorem effAnchor_congr {s s' : S3} {x : Nat} (h : s'.ancs x = s.ancs x) :
    s'.effAnchor x = s.effAnchor x := by simp only [S3.effAnchor, h]

/-- An anchor satisfying the rule of §44 has an existing effective anchor. -/
theorem effAnchorOK_get {s : S3} {x : Nat} {fd : Option Nat} (h : EffAnchorOK s x fd) :
    ∃ z, s.A[s.effAnchor x]? = some z := by
  unfold EffAnchorOK at h
  cases hz : s.A[s.effAnchor x]? with
  | none => rw [hz] at h; exact h.elim
  | some z => exact ⟨z, rfl⟩

/-- The effective anchor of an anchor satisfying the rule of §44 has a holder frame. -/
theorem effAnchorOK_frame {s : S3} {x : Nat} {fd : Option Nat} {z : Authority}
    (h : EffAnchorOK s x fd) (hz : s.A[s.effAnchor x]? = some z) :
    ∃ g, s.hframe z.holder = some g := by
  unfold EffAnchorOK at h; rw [hz] at h; simp only [OptP] at h
  cases hg : s.hframe z.holder with
  | none => rw [hg] at h; exact h.elim
  | some g => exact ⟨g, rfl⟩

/-- An anchor satisfying the rule of §44 is an authority of `A`. -/
theorem effAnchorOK_lt {s : S3} {x : Nat} {fd : Option Nat} (h : EffAnchorOK s x fd) :
    x < s.A.length := by
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := effAnchorOK_get h
  rcases effAnchor_mem s x with e | e
  · rw [e] at hz; exact lt_of_getElem? hz
  · have : s.org x ≠ none := fun ho => by rw [S3.ancs, chain_none ho] at e; simp at e
    simp only [S3.org] at this
    cases hx : s.A[x]? with
    | none => rw [hx] at this; exact absurd rfl this
    | some _ => exact lt_of_getElem? hx

/-- The rule of §44 carries over between states with the same holder frame of the effective
anchor and the same ancestor relation on the relevant frames. -/
theorem effAnchorOK_of_same {s s' : S3} {x x' : Nat} {z z' : Authority}
    (hz : s.A[s.effAnchor x]? = some z) (hz' : s'.A[s'.effAnchor x']? = some z')
    (hh : s'.hframe z'.holder = s.hframe z.holder) {fd fd' : Option Nat}
    (hanc : ∀ g f, fd = some f → (ancestor s'.F g f ↔ ancestor s.F g f)) (hfd : fd' = fd) :
    EffAnchorOK s' x' fd' ↔ EffAnchorOK s x fd := by
  rw [hfd]; unfold EffAnchorOK; rw [hz, hz']; simp only [OptP]; rw [hh]
  cases hg : s.hframe z.holder with
  | none => simp
  | some g =>
    cases hf : fd with
    | none => simp
    | some f => simp only; rw [hanc g f hf]

/-- Pushing a frame absent from the stack does not change the ancestors of a frame of the stack
(§39). -/
theorem ancestor_push {F : Frames} {n g f : Nat} (hn : n ≠ f) :
    ancestor (n :: F) g f ↔ ancestor F g f := by
  have hne : (n != f) = true := by simpa using hn
  show g ∈ (n :: F).dropWhile (· != f) ↔ g ∈ F.dropWhile (· != f)
  rw [List.dropWhile_cons]; simp only [hne, ↓reduceIte]

/-! ## Places and usability (§40) -/

/-- A part lies below the places it belongs to (§40, §49.2). -/
theorem partOf_le {P : List Place} {l r : Nat} (h : partOf P l r) : r ≤ l := by
  rcases h.2 with rfl | h
  · exact Nat.le_refl _
  · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt h)

/-- A usable place is not dead (§40, item 1). -/
theorem usable_dead {s : S3} {q : Nat} (h : s.Usable q) : s.dead q = false := by
  cases h <;> assumption

/-- The owner of a usable place is live (§40, items 2–3). -/
theorem usable_owner_live {s : S3} {q : Nat} {pl : Place} (h : s.Usable q)
    (hpl : s.P[q]? = some pl) : HolderLive s pl.owner := by
  cases h with
  | frame hp _ ho hf => rw [hpl] at hp; cases hp; rw [ho]; exact hf
  | place hp _ ho hu => rw [hpl] at hp; cases hp; rw [ho]; exact hu

/-- A place that exists, is not dead and has a live owner is usable (§40). -/
theorem usable_of_owner {s : S3} {q : Nat} {pl : Place} (hpl : s.P[q]? = some pl)
    (hd : s.dead q = false) (h : HolderLive s pl.owner) : s.Usable q := by
  cases ho : pl.owner with
  | frame f => rw [ho] at h; exact .frame hpl hd ho h
  | place o => rw [ho] at h; exact .place hpl hd ho h

/-! ## Places after `enterFrame` (§72 `ok` effect) -/

section Enter

variable {s : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape}

/-- The locals are appended to the places (§72 `ok` effect). -/
theorem enterP_len (s : S3) (ls : LocalShape) :
    (enterP s ls).length = s.P.length + ls.length := by
  simp [enterP, shapeP, toShape_length]

/-- Existing places are unchanged by `enterFrame` (§72 `ok` effect). -/
theorem enterP_lt {q : Nat} (h : q < s.P.length) : (enterP s ls)[q]? = s.P[q]? :=
  List.getElem?_append_left h

/-- Local `i` is the place `|P| + i`, owned by the new frame (§72 `ok` effect, §39). -/
theorem enterP_new {i : Nat} (h : i < ls.length) : (enterP s ls)[s.P.length + i]? =
    some ⟨(ls.toShape[i]?).bind (·.1), .frame s.nF, ((ls.toShape[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩ := by
  simp only [enterP, shapeP, List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_add_right _ _),
    Nat.add_sub_cancel_left, List.getElem?_map,
    List.getElem?_range (show i < ls.toShape.length by rw [toShape_length]; exact h),
    Option.map_some, shapeOwner_toShape]

effect). -/
theorem enterP_get {q : Nat} {pl : Place} (h : (enterP s ls)[q]? = some pl) :

514	      rcases hx0 with rfl | hx0

706	theorem enter_pframe_old (hwf : WF3 s) {q : Nat} (hq : q < s.P.length) :
707	    (enterEff s ps ls).pframe q = s.pframe q :=
708	  Option.ext fun f => by rw [pframe_iff, pframe_iff, enter_frameOf_old hwf hq]

710	/-- `enterFrame` preserves `AnchorOrder` (§44, §72): frames of existing places do not change, the
711	new frame is not an ancestor of an existing one, and an effective anchor, having no origin, is
712	never a parameter. -/
713	theorem enter_anchorOrder (hwf : WF3 s) (hao : AnchorOrder s) (hpre : EnterPre s ps ls) :
714	    AnchorOrder (enterEff s ps ls) := by
715	  intro q hq x hx
716	  by_cases hlt : q < s.P.length
717	  · have hq0 := enter_usable_back hwf hq hlt
718	    have hx0 : x ∈ s.D q := by simpa [enterEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega] using hx
719	    have hok := hao q hq0 x hx0
720	    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := effAnchorOK_get hok
721	    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := effAnchorOK_frame hok hz
722	    have hxl := effAnchorOK_lt hok
723	    have he : (enterEff s ps ls).effAnchor x = s.effAnchor x :=
724	      effAnchor_congr (enter_ancs_lt hxl)
725	    have hrl : s.effAnchor x < s.A.length := Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (effAnchor_le s x) hxl
726	    have hro : s.org (s.effAnchor x) = none := effAnchor_root hwf x
727	    have hnp : s.effAnchor x ∉ ps := fun hp => by
728	      have := hpre.params _ hp; simp only [OptP, hz] at this
729	      exact this.2.2 (by simpa [S3.org, hz] using hro)
730	    refine (effAnchorOK_of_same (s' := enterEff s ps ls) (z' := z) hz
731	      (by rw [he, enter_lt hrl, hz]; simp [hnp]) ?_ ?_ (enter_pframe_old hwf hlt)).2 hok
732	    · cases hh : z.holder with
733	      | frame f => rfl
734	      | place p =>
735	        rw [hh] at hg
736	        exact enter_pframe_old hwf (pframe_iff.1 hg).lt
737	    · intro g f hf
738	      obtain ⟨f', hf', hfF⟩ := hq0.frameOf
739	      rw [pframe_iff.2 hf'] at hf; rw [← Option.some.inj hf]
740	      exact ancestor_push fun e => Nat.lt_irrefl _ (e ▸ hwf.frames.2.2 _ hfF)
741	  · simp [enterEff, show s.P.length ≤ q by omega] at hx

743	/-- `enterFrame` preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §72): existing places keep their footprints and
744	their usability; a new root authority covers only its local, which is usable. -/
745	theorem enter_noDangling (hwf : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s) (hpre : EnterPre s ps ls) :
746	    NoDangling (enterEff s ps ls) := by
747	  intro j z hz za q hq l hl hlz
748	  obtain ⟨hlP, -, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
749	  have hql : q ≤ l := partOf_le hlq

750	  rcases enter_get hz with ⟨-, y, hy, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, i, -, rfl⟩
751	  · have hly : l ∈ y.footprint := by split at hlz <;> exact hlz
752	    have ya : y.active = true := by split at za <;> exact za
753	    have hqo : q < s.P.length := Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt hql (hwf.footprints j y hy l hly).1
754	    exact hnd j y hy ya q (fun hu => hq (enter_usable_old hu)) l
755	      ((enter_footprint_old hpre.localsOK hqo l).1 hl) hly
756	  · have hge : s.P.length ≤ l := enter_root_fp_ge hlz
757	    by_cases hqo : q < s.P.length
758	    · have := (mem_footprint.1 ((enter_footprint_old hpre.localsOK hqo l).1 hl)).1; omega
759	    · have hlP' : l < (enterP s ls).length := hlP
760	      rw [enterP_len] at hlP'
761	      have hu := enter_usable_new (s := s) (ps := ps) (ls := ls) (i := q - s.P.length) (by omega)
762	      rw [show s.P.length + (q - s.P.length) = q by omega] at hu
763	      exact hq hu

769	/-- The first surviving element of a list survives and belongs to it (§73.4). -/
770	theorem firstSurv_some {s : S3} {F₀ : Frames} {l : List Nat} {z : Nat}
771	    (h : firstSurv s F₀ l = some z) : z ∈ l ∧ Survives s F₀ z :=
772	  ⟨List.mem_of_find?_eq_some h, by simpa using List.find?_some h⟩

774	/-- No element of a list without first surviving element survives (§73.4). -/
775	theorem firstSurv_none {s : S3} {F₀ : Frames} {l : List Nat} (h : firstSurv s F₀ l = none) :
776	    ∀ w ∈ l, ¬ Survives s F₀ w := by
777	  intro w hw hs
778	  have := List.find?_eq_none.1 h w hw
779	  simp [hs] at this

781	/-- The first surviving strict ancestor (§73.4): an ancestor that survives, such that every
782	surviving ancestor is it or one of its own ancestors. -/
783	theorem firstSurv_ancs {s : S3} {F₀ : Frames} :
784	    ∀ n x, x < n → ∀ z, firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs x) = some z →
785	      z ∈ s.ancs x ∧ Survives s F₀ z ∧
786	        ∀ w ∈ s.ancs x, Survives s F₀ w → w = z ∨ w ∈ s.ancs z
787	  | 0, _, h, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
788	  | n + 1, x, hx, z, hz => by
789	    cases ho : s.org x with
790	    | none => rw [S3.ancs, chain_none ho] at hz; simp [firstSurv] at hz
791	    | some o =>
792	      obtain ⟨hlt, he⟩ : o < x ∧ s.ancs x = o :: s.ancs o := by
793	        rcases ancs_step ho with h | he
794	        · exact h
795	        · rw [he] at hz; simp [firstSurv] at hz
796	      rw [he] at hz ⊢
797	      by_cases hs : Survives s F₀ o
798	      · simp only [firstSurv, List.find?_cons_of_pos (p := fun z => decide (Survives s F₀ z))
799	          (by simpa using hs), Option.some.injEq] at hz
800	        subst hz
801	        refine ⟨List.mem_cons_self .., hs, fun w hw' _ => ?_⟩
802	        rcases List.mem_cons.1 hw' with rfl | hw'
803	        · exact .inl rfl
804	        · exact .inr hw'
805	      · simp only [firstSurv, List.find?_cons_of_neg (p := fun z => decide (Survives s F₀ z))
806	          (by simpa using hs)] at hz
807	        obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := firstSurv_ancs n o (by omega) z hz
808	        refine ⟨List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h1, h2, fun w hw' hws => ?_⟩
809	        rcases List.mem_cons.1 hw' with rfl | hw'
810	        · exact absurd hws hs
811	        · exact h3 w hw' hws

821	    (exitEff s).A[j]? = (s.A[j]?).map (exitG s s.F.tail j) := by
822	  simp [exitEff, getElem?_mapI]

825	theorem exit_get {j : Nat} {z : Authority} (hz : (exitEff s).A[j]? = some z) :
826	    ∃ z₀, s.A[j]? = some z₀ ∧ z = exitG s s.F.tail j z₀ := by
827	  rw [exit_A_get] at hz
828	  obtain ⟨z₀, hz₀, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hz
829	  exact ⟨z₀, hz₀, rfl⟩

832	(§73 `ok` effect, fourth item). -/
833	theorem exitG_same (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (a : Nat) (y : Authority) :
834	    (exitG s F₀ a y).mode = y.mode ∧ (exitG s F₀ a y).footprint = y.footprint ∧
835	    (exitG s F₀ a y).holder = y.holder := by
836	  unfold exitG; split
837	  · split <;> simp
838	  · simp

841	theorem exitG_active {F₀ : Frames} {a : Nat} {y : Authority} :
842	    (exitG s F₀ a y).active = true → Survives s F₀ a := by
843	  unfold exitG; split
844	  · intro; assumption
845	  · simp

847	/-- A surviving authority stays active (§73 `ok` effect). -/
848	theorem exitG_surv {F₀ : Frames} {a : Nat} {y : Authority} (hy : s.A[a]? = some y)
849	    (h : Survives s F₀ a) : (exitG s F₀ a y).active = true := by
850	  have hya : y.active = true := by unfold Survives at h; rw [hy] at h; exact h.1
851	  unfold exitG; simp only [h, ↓reduceIte]; split <;> simpa using hya

854	theorem exitG_active' {F₀ : Frames} {a : Nat} {y : Authority} (hy : s.A[a]? = some y)

856	  have := exitG_active h; unfold Survives at this; rw [hy] at this; exact this.1

858	/-- The origin after the exit is unchanged, or it is the first surviving ancestor of a surviving
859	derived authority (§73 `ok` effect, third item). -/
860	theorem exitG_origin {F₀ : Frames} {a : Nat} {y : Authority} :
861	    (exitG s F₀ a y).origin = y.origin ∨
862	    (Survives s F₀ a ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ (exitG s F₀ a y).origin = firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a)) := by
863	  unfold exitG; split
864	  · rename_i hs; split
865	    · exact .inl rfl
866	    · rename_i o ho; exact .inr ⟨hs, by simp [ho], rfl⟩
867	  · exact .inl rfl

869	/-- After the exit, surviving ancestors of an authority are still its ancestors (§73.4). -/
870	theorem exit_ancs_keep :
871	    ∀ n x, x < n → ∀ w ∈ s.ancs x, Survives s s.F.tail w → w ∈ (exitEff s).ancs x
872	  | 0, _, h, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
873	  | n + 1, x, hx, w, hw', hws => by
874	    cases hy : s.A[x]? with
875	    | none =>
876	      have : s.org x = none := by simp [S3.org, hy]
877	      rw [S3.ancs, chain_none this] at hw'; simp at hw'
878	    | some y =>
879	      cases ho : y.origin with
880	      | none =>
881	        have : s.org x = none := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
882	        rw [S3.ancs, chain_none this] at hw'; simp at hw'
883	      | some o =>
884	        have hob : s.org x = some o := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
885	        obtain ⟨hlt, hax⟩ : o < x ∧ s.ancs x = o :: s.ancs o := by
886	          rcases ancs_step hob with h | hax
887	          · exact h
888	          · rw [hax] at hw'; simp at hw'
889	        have e' : (exitEff s).org x = (exitG s s.F.tail x y).origin := by
890	          simp [S3.org, exit_A_get, hy]
891	        rcases exitG_origin (s := s) (F₀ := s.F.tail) (a := x) (y := y) with e | ⟨-, -, e⟩
892	        · rw [e, ho] at e'
893	          rw [show (exitEff s).ancs x = o :: (exitEff s).ancs o from chain_cons e' hlt]
894	          rw [hax] at hw'
895	          rcases List.mem_cons.1 hw' with rfl | hw'
896	          · exact List.mem_cons_self ..
897	          · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (exit_ancs_keep n o (by omega) w hw' hws)
898	        · rw [e] at e'
899	          cases hz : firstSurv s s.F.tail (s.ancs x) with
900	          | none => exact absurd hws (firstSurv_none hz w hw')
901	          | some z =>
902	            rw [hz] at e'
903	            obtain ⟨hz1, -, hz3⟩ := firstSurv_ancs (x + 1) x (Nat.lt_succ_self x) z hz
904	            have hzx := chain_lt hz1
905	            rw [show (exitEff s).ancs x = z :: (exitEff s).ancs z from chain_cons e' hzx]
906	            rcases hz3 w hw' hws with rfl | hw''
907	            · exact List.mem_cons_self ..
908	            · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (exit_ancs_keep n z (by omega) w hw'' hws)

911	abbrev OriginsSurvive (s : S3) : Prop :=
912	  ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives s s.F.tail a → s.org a ≠ none →
913	    firstSurv s s.F.tail (s.ancs a) ≠ none

915	/-- The root of an origin chain stays on the chain after the exit (§73.4), when every surviving
916	derived authority has a surviving origin. -/
917	theorem exit_root_kept (h3 : OriginsSurvive s) :
918	    ∀ n a, a < n → ∀ x0, x0 ∈ s.ancs a → s.org x0 = none → x0 ∈ (exitEff s).ancs a
919	  | 0, _, h, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
920	  | n + 1, a, ha, x0, hx0, hx0o => by
921	    cases hy : s.A[a]? with
922	    | none =>
923	      have : s.org a = none := by simp [S3.org, hy]
924	      rw [S3.ancs, chain_none this] at hx0; simp at hx0
925	    | some y =>
926	      cases ho : y.origin with
927	      | none =>
928	        have : s.org a = none := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
929	        rw [S3.ancs, chain_none this] at hx0; simp at hx0
930	      | some o =>
931	        have hob : s.org a = some o := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
932	        obtain ⟨hlt, hax⟩ : o < a ∧ s.ancs a = o :: s.ancs o := by
933	          rcases ancs_step hob with h | hax
934	          · exact h
935	          · rw [hax] at hx0; simp at hx0
936	        have e' : (exitEff s).org a = (exitG s s.F.tail a y).origin := by
937	          simp [S3.org, exit_A_get, hy]
938	        rcases exitG_origin (s := s) (F₀ := s.F.tail) (a := a) (y := y) with e | ⟨hsv, -, e⟩
939	        · rw [e, ho] at e'
940	          rw [show (exitEff s).ancs a = o :: (exitEff s).ancs o from chain_cons e' hlt]
941	          rw [hax] at hx0
942	          rcases List.mem_cons.1 hx0 with rfl | hx0
943	          · exact List.mem_cons_self ..
944	          · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (exit_root_kept h3 n o (by omega) x0 hx0 hx0o)
945	        · rw [e] at e'
946	          cases hz : firstSurv s s.F.tail (s.ancs a) with
947	          | none =>
948	            exact absurd hz (h3 a (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) hsv (by rw [hob]; simp))
949	          | some z =>
950	            rw [hz] at e'
951	            have hz1 := (firstSurv_some hz).1
952	            have hzx := chain_lt hz1
953	            rw [show (exitEff s).ancs a = z :: (exitEff s).ancs z from chain_cons e' hzx]
954	            rcases ancs_root_after (a + 1) a (Nat.lt_succ_self a) z x0 hz1 hx0 hx0o with rfl | hx'
955	            · exact List.mem_cons_self ..
956	            · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (exit_root_kept h3 n z (by omega) x0 hx' hx0o)

958	/-- The root of the origin chain of a surviving authority survives (§73.4), when every surviving
959	derived authority has a surviving origin. -/
960	theorem exit_root_survives (h3 : OriginsSurvive s) :
961	    ∀ n a, a < n → Survives s s.F.tail a → ∀ x0, (x0 = a ∨ x0 ∈ s.ancs a) → s.org x0 = none →
962	      Survives s s.F.tail x0
963	  | 0, _, h, _, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
964	  | n + 1, a, ha, hs, x0, hx0, hx0o => by
965	    rcases hx0 with rfl | hx0
966	    · exact hs
967	    have hA : a < s.A.length := by
968	      unfold Survives OptP at hs; split at hs
969	      · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
970	      · exact hs.elim
971	    have horg : s.org a ≠ none := fun e => by rw [S3.ancs, chain_none e] at hx0; simp at hx0
972	    cases hz : firstSurv s s.F.tail (s.ancs a) with
973	    | none => exact absurd hz (h3 a (List.mem_range.2 hA) hs horg)
974	    | some z =>
975	      obtain ⟨hz1, hzs⟩ := firstSurv_some hz
976	      rcases ancs_root_after (a + 1) a (Nat.lt_succ_self a) z x0 hz1 hx0 hx0o with rfl | hx'
977	      · exact hzs
978	      · exact exit_root_survives h3 n z (by have := chain_lt hz1; omega) hzs x0 (.inr hx') hx0o

982	    (exitEff s).Usable q ↔ ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q :=

986	theorem usable_of_tail {q : Nat} (h : ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q) : s.Usable q :=
987	  S3.Usable.mono (s := s) (s' := ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3)) rfl

990	/-- Conservation along an origin chain (§51): a derived authority has a mode not exceeding, and a
991	footprint within, those of every ancestor. -/
992	theorem i2_chain (h2 : I2 s) :
993	    ∀ n b, b < n → ∀ (y : Authority) z, s.A[b]? = some y → z ∈ s.ancs b →
994	      ∃ x : Authority, s.A[z]? = some x ∧ y.mode.le x.mode ∧ ∀ p ∈ y.footprint, p ∈ x.footprint
995	  | 0, _, h, _, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
996	  | n + 1, b, hb, y, z, hy, hz => by
997	    cases ho : y.origin with
998	    | none =>
999	      have : s.org b = none := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
1000	      rw [S3.ancs, chain_none this] at hz; simp at hz
1001	    | some o =>
1002	      have hob : s.org b = some o := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
1003	      obtain ⟨hlt, he⟩ : o < b ∧ s.ancs b = o :: s.ancs o := by
1004	        rcases ancs_step hob with h | he
1005	        · exact h
1006	        · rw [he] at hz; simp at hz
1007	      rw [he] at hz
1008	      obtain ⟨x, hx, hm, hh⟩ := h2 b y o hy ho
1009	      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hz with rfl | hz
1010	      · exact ⟨x, hx, hm, hh⟩
1011	      · obtain ⟨x', hx', hm', hh'⟩ := i2_chain h2 n o (by omega) x z hx hz
1012	        exact ⟨x', hx', Mode.le_trans hm hm', fun p hp => hh' p (hh p hp)⟩

1016	/-- `exitFrame` preserves `RootChain` (§49.6, §73.4): reanchoring keeps the root of every chain. -/
1017	theorem exit_rootChain (hc : RootChain s) (h3 : OriginsSurvive s) : RootChain (exitEff s) := by
1018	  intro a y l ha hl hleaf
1019	  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, rfl⟩ := exit_get ha
1020	  rw [(exitG_same s s.F.tail a y₀).2.1] at hl
1021	  obtain ⟨x0, z, r, hx0, hz, hzo, hr, hlr, hfz⟩ := hc a y₀ l hy₀ hl hleaf
1022	  have hx0o : s.org x0 = none := by simp [S3.org, hz, hzo]
1023	  refine ⟨x0, exitG s s.F.tail x0 z, r, ?_, by rw [exit_A_get, hz]; rfl, ?_, hr, hlr,
1024	    fun l' => by rw [(exitG_same s s.F.tail x0 z).2.1]; exact hfz l'⟩
1025	  · rcases hx0 with rfl | hx0
1026	    · exact .inl rfl
1027	    · exact .inr (exit_root_kept h3 (a + 1) a (Nat.lt_succ_self a) x0 hx0 hx0o)
1028	  · rcases exitG_origin (s := s) (F₀ := s.F.tail) (a := x0) (y := z) with e | ⟨-, hn, -⟩
1029	    · rw [e]; exact hzo
1030	    · exact absurd hzo hn

1033	usable is held by the live owner of that place, so it survives unchanged. -/
1034	theorem exit_rootHeld (h : RootHeld s) : RootHeld (exitEff s) := by
1035	  intro r hrp hur
1036	  have hu' : ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable r := exit_usable_iff.1 hur
1037	  obtain ⟨i, z, pr, hz, za, zo, zm, hpr, hzh, hzf⟩ := h r hrp (usable_of_tail hu')
1038	  have hlive : HolderLive { s with F := s.F.tail } z.holder := by
1039	    rw [hzh]; exact usable_owner_live hu' hpr
1040	  have hsv : Survives s s.F.tail i := by unfold Survives; rw [hz]; exact ⟨za, hlive⟩
1041	  refine ⟨i, z, pr, ?_, za, zo, zm, hpr, hzh, hzf⟩
1042	  rw [exit_A_get, hz]; unfold exitG; simp [hsv, zo]

1044	/-- `exitFrame` preserves `WF3` (§49, §73): the caller survives and the stack shrinks; places
1045	are unchanged; reanchored origins are earlier ancestors; active authorities survive, so their

/-- Places `P` followed by the elements of a shape (§47, §71, §72): (parent, owning element,
kind), owned by their owning element or by `hd`. -/
def shapeP (P : List Place) (hd : Holder) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    List Place :=
  P ++ (List.range ls.length).map fun i =>
    ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), shapeOwner ls hd i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩

/-- Well-formed shape at offset `n` (§72.2, §71.1; for statics, the hypothesis recorded for
§47): the parent and the owning element of an element are earlier elements, and a part has the
owning element of its parent. -/
def ShapeOK (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i ∈ List.range ls.length,
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)) (fun r => n ≤ r ∧ r < n + i ∧
      (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = (ls[r - n]?).bind (·.2.1)) True ∧
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1)) (fun o => n ≤ o ∧ o < n + i) True

/-- Decidability of `ShapeOK` (§72.2, §71.1). -/
instance (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (ShapeOK n ls) := by
  unfold ShapeOK; infer_instance

/-- Indices of the root elements (no parent) of a shape (§40 root places; §47, §71, §72). -/
def rootIdx (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Nat :=
  (List.range ls.length).filter fun i => ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)).isNone

/-! ## O6 `enterFrame` (§72) -/

/-- Places after `enterFrame` (§72, `ok` effect): the locals appended, owned by the new frame. -/
def enterP (s : S3) (ls : LocalShape) : List Place := shapeP s.P (.frame s.nF) ls.toShape

/-- Effect of `enterFrame(params, locals)` (§72, `ok` effect): a new frame `nF` is pushed; the
parameters are now held by it; locals are appended (uninitialized, no anchor, alive) with one
active root `Modify` authority per root local, held by the new frame; pinning obligations are
unchanged. -/
def enterEff (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : S3 :=
  { F := s.nF :: s.F, nF := s.nF + 1, P := enterP s ls
    I := fun l => if s.P.length ≤ l then .uninit else s.I l
    A := mapI (fun j y => if j ∈ ps then { y with holder := .frame s.nF } else y) 0 s.A ++
      (rootIdx ls.toShape).map fun i =>
        ⟨.modify, none, footprint (enterP s ls) (s.P.length + i),
          shapeOwner ls.toShape (.frame s.nF) i, true⟩
    D := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.dead q
    pins := s.pins }

/-- Origin protection on entry for parameter `p` in state `s'` (§72.3): if `p` is a `Modify`
authority with direct origin `o`, `o` is exercisable in no mode. -/
def ParamOriginHidden (s' : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s'.A[p]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify →
    OptP y.origin (fun o => ¬ s'.ExercisableAt o .observe ∧ ¬ s'.ExercisableAt o .modify) True) True

/-- Decidability of `ParamOriginHidden` (§72.3). -/
instance (s' : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (ParamOriginHidden s' p) := by
  unfold ParamOriginHidden; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `enterFrame` (§72). The modes/footprints/parameter-passing part of §72.2 is
not represented. -/
structure EnterPre (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : Prop where
  /-- §72.1: the calling frame, the current frame, is live. -/
  callerLive : s.F ≠ []
  /-- §72.1: each parameter is an active derived authority held by the caller. -/
  params : ∀ a ∈ ps, OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.holder = .frame s.top ∧
    y.origin ≠ none) False
  /-- §72.2: the locals form a well-formed shape (each parent is an earlier local). -/
  localsOK : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape
  /-- §72.3: origin protection on entry, in the resulting state. -/
  originHidden : ∀ p ∈ ps, ParamOriginHidden (enterEff s ps ls) p
  /-- §72.4: `AnchorOrderHeld` over the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld (enterEff s ps ls)

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `enterFrame` (§72). -/
instance (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : Decidable (EnterPre s ps ls) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.F ≠ [] ∧ (∀ a ∈ ps, OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧
      y.holder = .frame s.top ∧ y.origin ≠ none) False) ∧ ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape ∧
    (∀ p ∈ ps, ParamOriginHidden (enterEff s ps ls) p) ∧ AnchorOrderHeld (enterEff s ps ls))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩⟩

/-- `enterFrame` as a relation (§72). -/
def EnterStep (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EnterPre s ps ls) (enterEff s ps ls)

/-! ## O7 `exitFrame` (§73) -/

/-- Authority `x` survives the exit to stack `F₀` (§73.4): active and held by a surviving frame
or by a usable place whose terminal owner survives. -/
def Survives (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ HolderLive { s with F := F₀ } y.holder) False

/-- Decidability of `Survives` (§73.4). -/
instance (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (x : Nat) : Decidable (Survives s F₀ x) := by
  unfold Survives; infer_instance

/-- First surviving authority of a list (§73.4). -/
def firstSurv (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (l : List Nat) : Option Nat :=
  l.find? fun z => decide (Survives s F₀ z)

/-- Authority `a` after the exit (§73, `ok` effect): released unless it survives; a surviving
derived authority is reanchored to the first surviving active origin of its chain. -/
def exitG (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (a : Nat) (y : Authority) : Authority :=
  if Survives s F₀ a then
    match y.origin with
    | none => y
    | some _ => { y with origin := firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a) }
  else { y with active := false }

/-- Effect of `exitFrame` (§73, `ok` effect): the current frame is popped; authorities that do
not survive are released; surviving derived authorities and the anchors of `D` are reanchored to
the first surviving authority of their chains. -/
def exitEff (s : S3) : S3 :=
  { s with
    F := s.F.tail
    D := fun q => (s.D q).map fun x => (firstSurv s s.F.tail (x :: s.ancs x)).getD x
    A := mapI (exitG s s.F.tail) 0 s.A }

/-- Preconditions of `exitFrame` (§73). The result clause of §73.2 is not represented. -/
structure ExitPre (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop where
  /-- §73.1: the current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller. -/
  hasCaller : s.F.tail ≠ []
  /-- §73.2, §73.4, §73.5: every anchor of a place usable after the exit has a surviving
  authority among itself and its origins. -/
  anchors : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ s.D q, firstSurv s s.F.tail (x :: s.ancs x) ≠ none
  /-- §73.4: every surviving derived authority has a surviving active origin. -/
  origins : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives s s.F.tail a → s.org a ≠ none →
    firstSurv s s.F.tail (s.ancs a) ≠ none
  /-- §73.3: no leaf of a place that dies with the frame is pinned, statically or
  dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q →
    ¬ ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l
  /-- §73.5: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld (exitEff s)

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `exitFrame` (§73). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) : Decidable (ExitPre k s) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.F.tail ≠ [] ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
      ∀ x ∈ s.D q, firstSurv s s.F.tail (x :: s.ancs x) ≠ none) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives s s.F.tail a → s.org a ≠ none →
      firstSurv s s.F.tail (s.ancs a) ≠ none) ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ¬ ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l) ∧
    AnchorOrderHeld (exitEff s))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩⟩

/-- `exitFrame` as a relation (§73). -/
def ExitStep (k : K) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop := Guarded (ExitPre k s) (exitEff s)

/-! ## O9 `read`, O10 `write`, O11 `writeShared` (§66–§68) -/

/-- Leaf `l` belongs to a usable place (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1). -/
def LeafOfUsable (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q ∧ l ∈ footprint s.P q

/-- Decidability of `LeafOfUsable` (§66.1). -/
instance (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Decidable (LeafOfUsable s l) := by
  unfold LeafOfUsable; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `read` of the leaves `ls` through `access` (§66). The type and storage
contract of §66.3 is not represented. -/

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

----
## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

----
## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

-----
## 72. O6 — Entering a Frame

**Preconditions**

1. The calling frame is the current frame and is live. Each parameter passed to the callee is an active, derived authority held by the caller before the step; the caller is **not necessarily** the frame in which the authority was first derived.
2. Modes, footprints, anchoring, and parameter-passing rules permit this change of holder; introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots.
3. **Origin protection on entry:** for each `Modify` parameter with direct origin `o`, `o` is exercisable in **no mode** (neither `Observe` nor `Modify`) in the **resulting state**, once the new frame's parameters and locals have been created.
4. **G4:** `AnchorOrderHeld` is checked over the complete resulting state.

**`ok` effect:** A new child frame is pushed onto the stack; active parameters **are yielded** to that frame, which becomes their sole holder; local places and their root authorities are created; valid anchors inherited from the caller are preserved. This transfer creates no additional rights. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

This clause establishes **entry protection**. It does not prove the stronger property of protection throughout the **entire** invocation following other releases or reanchorings. While a `Modify` parameter remains active, its direct origin remains subject to effective-mode restrictions. Any additional protection throughout the invocation is deferred to Spec 3.

## 73. O7 — Exiting a Frame

**Preconditions**

1. The current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller.
2. Results that must survive have already been legally transferred to their destinations; no active authority or dependency may remain invalidly attached to locals that are about to die.
3. **No leaf of a place that dies with the frame, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`).
4. Iterated reanchoring of surviving authorities and anchors reaches the **first surviving active origin**, held either by a surviving frame or by a usable place whose terminal owner survives; it is not permitted to skip a surviving origin merely because it is held by a place. The operation is rejected when no suitable surviving origin exists, particularly if the chain reaches a root of the exiting frame.
5. Validity of anchors of surviving values and `AnchorOrderHeld` are checked **in the resulting state**. Other state invariants and resource contracts are respected.

**`ok` effect:**

- the current frame is removed from the stack; its untransferred locals and substorages dying with them become unusable;
- authorities still held by that frame, or by places that have become unusable, are released;
- origins of surviving derived authorities are reanchored to the **first surviving active origin** of their chains, whether held by a frame or a usable place, and the `D` anchors of surviving values are correspondingly reanchored;
- reanchoring changes **neither the footprint nor the own mode** of an authority; parameter identities and relations specific to the frame cease their operational role;
- the calling frame becomes current again.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places. Deferred cleanup (`defer`) lies outside this kernel. Reanchoring may change the current `origin` relation; protection of a historical borrow lineage during an invocation is a distinct, deferred question.

# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments

Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.

## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation of fresh identity is installed on the relevant leaves. A leaf is dynamically pinned while at least one active pinning obligation covers it. While an obligation is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `unpin` designates one active dynamic pinning obligation, installed by `pin` on `place`; `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone`, applied to that obligation, attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The designated dynamic pinning obligation ends, and only that one: a leaf it covered stays pinned while another active obligation covers it. The step does not itself modify values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.

## Follow-up answers (verbatim, French)

Q9 (suite) : règle unifiée. endUse et free sont rejetés si une autorité qu'ils désactivent — détenue par un emplacement qui meurt, stockage possédé transitivement compris, ou racine d'un stockage libéré — a un descendant actif, quelle que soit son empreinte, que le même pas ne désactive pas. Les cas (1) et (2) sont donc rejetés. La sortie de cadre garde son ré-ancrage, et rejette si aucune origine survivante n'existe (inchangé). I2 au sens « origine active » tient après chaque pas.

Q3 (suite) : remplace Q17. Dans §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3, sont exemptées des contrôles « autorité dérivée active couvrant depuis l'extérieur » les autorités par lesquelles le pas exerce son droit Modify : l'autorité exerçable qui fonde le droit et sa chaîne d'origines (pour le pool : entrée, compagne, internal et ses origines). Les autres autorités actives restent contrôlées. Le témoin Q3 (1) devient : resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de l'entrée vers un local, unresolve, freeSlot accepté, y compris avec internal dérivé. W1 suit le même chemin. Réévaluer W2 sous cette lecture. Ajouter §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3 aux amendements de la v0.1.

(Cases (1) and (2) above refer to: (1) endUse(p) where p owns an allocation q holding a stored authority a, the frame holding b derived from a over another static; (2) free(p) with an empty-footprint derivative of p's root held by the frame.)

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Lemmas

/-!
# Access kernel: the preserved invariant

The conjunction that every kernel step must preserve (§57 of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`) and the auxiliary invariant carried with it. The per-operation preservation modules state their results with these two predicates.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- The kernel invariant of §57: `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`. -/
def KInv (s : S3) : Prop := WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧ NoOrphan s

/-- Auxiliary invariant carried with `KInv`, not a clause of §57 (§40, §49.7): the converse
root-holder property `RootHeldConv`, which is not a clause of `WF3`. -/
def KAux (s : S3) : Prop := RootHeldConv s

/-- `NoOrphan` follows from `WF3` (§54, §49.7), so `KInv` reduces to its first three
conjuncts. -/
theorem kInv_of {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hi : Inv3 s) (ha : AnchorOrderHeld s) : KInv s :=
  ⟨hw, hi, ha, noOrphan_of_wf3 hw⟩

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- An active derived authority of the resulting state held by place `q` is an anchor of `q`
(§44), or it was already such an authority before the step and the step keeps the anchors of `q`
when `q` was usable (§52). Under `WF3` (§49.8) this gives `HeldAnchored` after the step. -/
private theorem heldAnchored_of_step {s s' : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hh : HeldAnchored s)
    (hstep : ∀ x y q, s'.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
      y.holder = .place q → x ∈ s'.D q ∨ ∃ y₀ : Authority, s.A[x]? = some y₀ ∧
        y₀.active = true ∧ y₀.origin ≠ none ∧ y₀.holder = .place q ∧
        (s.Usable q → x ∈ s.D q → x ∈ s'.D q)) : HeldAnchored s' := by
  intro x y q hy ya ho hhq _
  rcases hstep x y q hy ya ho hhq with h | ⟨y₀, hy₀, ya₀, ho₀, hh₀, himp⟩
  · exact h
  · have hu : s.Usable q := by have := hw.holders x y₀ hy₀ ya₀; rw [hh₀] at this; exact this
    exact himp hu (hh x y₀ q hy₀ ya₀ ho₀ hh₀ hu)

/-- An element of an appended list comes from one of the two parts (§42: authorities added by
`derive`, `split`, `enterFrame`, `alloc`). -/
private theorem getElem?_append_cases {α : Type} {l E : List α} {x : Nat} {y : α}
    (h : (l ++ E)[x]? = some y) : l[x]? = some y ∨ y ∈ E := by
  by_cases hx : x < l.length
  · rw [List.getElem?_append_left hx] at h; exact .inl h
  · rw [List.getElem?_append_right (by omega)] at h; exact .inr (List.mem_of_getElem? h)

/-- Every operation preserves `HeldAnchored` from a `WF3` state (§44; §60–§75 `ok` effects): new
authorities are held by frames or have no origin; `store` anchors what it stores (§65); a
`transfer` moves an authority with the anchors of its holder (§63); `exitFrame` maps a surviving
anchor to itself (§73); the other steps only release authorities or keep the anchors of the
places whose authorities stay active. -/

/-! ## Preservation of `I5` (§57, §72, §73) -/

/-- `enterFrame` preserves `I5` (§57; §72 `ok` effect): the pinning obligations are unchanged,
and an existing usable place stays usable with the same footprint. -/
theorem enter_preserves_i5 {k : K} {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (h5 : I5 k s)
    (h : EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s')) : I5 k s' := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  intro l hl
  rw [S3.pin_congr (pins_enterEff s ps ls)] at hl
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hlq⟩ := h5 l hl
  exact ⟨q, Frames.enter_usable_old hq, (Frames.enter_footprint_old hpre.localsOK hq.lt l).2 hlq⟩

/-- `exitFrame` preserves `I5` (§57; §73.3, §73 `ok` effect): the pinning obligations and the
places are unchanged, and a usable place that becomes unusable has no pinned leaf (§73.3). -/
theorem exit_preserves_i5 {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h5 : I5 k s) (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) :
    I5 k s' := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  intro l hl
  rw [S3.pin_congr (pins_exitEff s)] at hl
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hlq⟩ := h5 l hl
  by_cases hu : ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3).Usable q
  · exact ⟨q, Frames.exit_usable_iff.2 hu, hlq⟩
  · have hnp := hpre.notPinned q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq hu l hlq
    rcases hl with hk | hp
    · exact absurd hk hnp.2
    · rw [hnp.1] at hp; cases hp

input.summary:
Frames.lean now elaborates against the v0.1 definitions, checked with `cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Preserve/Frames.lean`. There are no errors and no warnings, and the file has no sorry, admit, native_decide, axiom, noncomputable or set_option. I ran `#print axioms` on all 110 declarations of the file through a scratch copy in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref/v01/frames-ax/FramesAx.lean. Each one uses only {propext} or {propext, Quot.sound}; none uses Classical.choice.

Spec passages covered (specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md): §51 (I2, an active derived authority has an active origin), §57 (I5), §72 (enterFrame), §73.3, §73.4 and the §73 `ok` effect (exitFrame), and §74 (a leaf is pinned while an active obligation covers it).

Only two kinds of break came from stage 1: the new active-origin conjunct of I2, and the new I5 obligation. The pins redesign changed nothing else here: both steps leave `pins` unchanged (`pins_enterEff`, `pins_exitEff`).

- **KInv for enterFrame:** a parameter changes only its holder, so the activity of both an authority and its origin carries over unchanged.
- **KInv for exitFrame:** an authority that is active after the exit survives. Its origin is then its first surviving ancestor. That ancestor survives too, so it is still active after the exit. No new hypothesis was needed.
- **KAux:** the existing proofs are unchanged.
- **I5:** both lemmas need no invariant hypothesis on s; the reasons are in the theorem lines below.

No statement of an existing theorem changed, nothing was deleted, and no new auxiliary invariant was needed for these two operations. I also updated the module header to name the v0.1 spec and to list I5.

Theorems:
- ADDED `Frames.exitG_origin_surv`, Frames.lean:874. For an authority that survives the exit, a new origin `some o` means `o` is the first surviving ancestor of its chain (§73 `ok` effect, third item; §73.4). This is a helper inside the `Frames` namespace.
- ADDED `enter_preserves_i5`, Frames.lean:1281: `I5 k s → EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s') → I5 k s'` (§57, §72). Pins are unchanged, existing usable places stay usable (`enter_usable_old`), and their footprints are unchanged (`enter_footprint_old` with `hpre.localsOK`).
- ADDED `exit_preserves_i5`, Frames.lean:1291: `I5 k s → ExitStep k s (.ok s') → I5 k s'` (§57; §73.3). Pins and places are unchanged. A usable place that becomes unusable has no pinned leaf, by `ExitPre.notPinned` (§73.3).
- RE-PROVED, statement unchanged, `Frames.enter_inv3base`, Frames.lean:663: adds the active conjunct of I2 (§51).
- RE-PROVED, statement unchanged, `Frames.exit_inv3base`, Frames.lean:1098: adds the active conjunct of I2 (§51, §73.4); docstring extended.
- RE-PROVED, statement unchanged, `Frames.i2_chain`, Frames.lean:1004: it now ignores the new conjunct of I2.
- UNCHANGED and still elaborating: `enter_preserves` (Frames.lean:1245), `exit_preserves` (1262), `enter_preserves_kAux`, `exit_preserves_kAux`, `enterStep_det`, `exitStep_det`, `exit_keeps_base`, `enter_keeps_base`, `exitFrame_frame_gone`, `exitFrame_releases_all`, `exitFrame_no_dangling`, `exitFrame_reanchors`, `exitFrame_reanchors_anchors`, `enter_yields`, `param_origin_restricted`, `call_params_effective_protected`, `enter_params_protected`, `Frames.Witness.w7_reachable`, `Frames.Witness.exit_reanchors_to_place_witness`, and every helper in the `Frames` namespace.
- REMOVED: none.
